audit_scope.description: This audit covers EL gas economics and block validation (EIP-7935), CL data availability via polynomial commitment sampling (Fulu PCS), and the Pectra fork activation lifecycle (EIP-7600) spanning both EL and CL.

out_of_scope_reasons.Mainnet/Testnet Testing: All testing should be done on local forks of testnet or mainnet
out_of_scope_reasons.Pricing Oracles: Incorrect data supplied by third party oracles (oracle manipulation/flash loan attacks are in-scope)
out_of_scope_reasons.Third-party Smart Contracts: Any testing with third-party systems and applications is prohibited
out_of_scope_reasons.Test Files: Impacts on test files and configuration files unless stated otherwise
out_of_scope_reasons.Configuration Files: Impacts on test files and configuration files unless stated otherwise
out_of_scope_reasons.Privileged Access: Impacts caused by attacks requiring access to privileged addresses without additional modifications are out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.Centralization Risks: Impacts involving centralization risks are out-of-scope

misclassified_entities.reason: The Data Availability Sampler is an internal CL component responsible for collecting cells from the network. It is not an external entity — the true external source is the network peer providing the cells. Reclassified to use EXT-NETWORK-PEER as the external entity for recovery inputs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer / Validator
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block production pipeline (gas limit configuration read, block header construction)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers are validators who may be adversarial. They control block contents within protocol rules and could construct worst-case blocks to maximize resource consumption. No implicit trust.

trusted_external_entities.name: Adversarial Block Builder
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: CL gossip network (block propagation via P2P)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Malicious block builder constructing worst-case blocks to maximize serialized size and stress CL gossip limits. Fully untrusted — blocks must be validated against the 10 MiB gossip limit.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External users submitting transactions. Completely untrusted — transactions must be validated against block gas limit and any per-transaction gas cap.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Producer (Validator/Beacon Node)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Blob submission for encoding into cells (internal CL pipeline)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Blob data originates from validators or beacon nodes. Authenticated via CL protocol, but blob content must still be validated (length checks, field element range). SEMI_TRUSTED because the channel is authenticated but content is not implicitly valid.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer (Cell/Proof Provider)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P network (cell, proof, and commitment gossip)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Untrusted peer nodes providing cells, KZG proofs, and commitments over the P2P network. All data must undergo full validation: byte length checks, index bound checks, BLS subgroup checks, field element range validation, and KZG proof verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Peer Node via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: malicious peer sending invalid blocks or transactions via devp2p. Eclipse attacks, invalid block propagation. Fully untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via CL P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: malicious validator proposing invalid blocks, conflicting attestations, or withholding data. Fully untrusted despite being a protocol participant.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block header gas limit field (block production)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block gas limit must be validated against protocol rules (1/1024 adjustment bound from parent). Producers cannot set arbitrary gas limits — the EL must enforce the gas limit voting mechanism constraints.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: CL gossip message validation (10 MiB limit)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: CL must reject blocks exceeding the 10 MiB gossip message size limit. At 60M gas, worst-case blocks should remain well below this limit (threshold is ~150M gas). The CL must enforce this check before propagating blocks.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction validation (gas limit check against block gas limit and per-tx cap)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: gas limit must not exceed block gas limit (60M), signature validation, nonce validation, balance checks. If a per-transaction gas cap exists, it must also be enforced.
Blob length must equal BYTES_PER_BLOB exactly. Even though the producer is semi-trusted (authenticated channel), the encoding pipeline must validate input length before processing.

All inputs must be validated: byte lengths for commitments (BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT), proofs (BYTES_PER_PROOF), cells (BYTES_PER_CELL); cell indices < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB; BLS subgroup membership for deserialized group elements; field element values < BLS_MODULUS. Only after all validation passes should cryptographic verification proceed.

Recovery inputs must be validated: cell count >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2, no duplicate indices, ascending order, all indices < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, each cell length == BYTES_PER_CELL. Cells used for recovery originate from untrusted peers and must have been previously verified via KZG proof verification.

All blocks and transactions received via P2P must undergo full validation identical to locally-produced content. Invalid blocks must be rejected and peers may be penalized. Eclipse attack mitigations (peer diversity, connection limits) must be in place.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Beacon P2P gossip validation (block proposals, attestations)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All block proposals must be validated against consensus rules. Conflicting attestations must trigger slashing conditions. Data availability must be verified via PeerDAS sampling. Invalid proposals must be rejected and the validator penalized.
